With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by award dated 28.07.2023 passed by 20th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur in MACC No. 2727/2016 seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

entities.text: 20th Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to medical evidence on record as well as impugned award, submits that as per medical evidence appellant has suffered 59% permanent disability.
But Tribunal has wrongly determined permanent disability as 24%.

Further, Tribunal has determined appellant's monthly income Rs.5,000/- per month whereas on the date of accident,
minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.6850/-.
Further, Tribunal has not awarded sufficient amount under heads for pain and suffering, nourishing diet and conveyance charges etc.

On above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by the tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4.
Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
Hence, no enhancement is required.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

So far as percentage of permanent disability is concerned, it is correct that as per medical evidence, appellant suffered 59% permanent disability and tribunal has assessed loss of earning capacity/permanent disability in relation to whole body as 24%.
7.
Perusal of deposition of applicant Gajraj Uikey reveal that he has not specifically mentioned about nature/details/extent of permanent disability suffered by him in left hand.
Further, appellant has filed disability certificate (Ex.P/52) but it has not examined the concerned doctor.
In Ex.P/52, it is mentioned that it is a case of locomotor disability and restricted ROM elbow.

8. Hence, in view of nature of evidence available on record with respect to permanent disability, it cannot be said that tribunal has wrongly determined loss of future earning capacity as 24%.
Gajraj Uikey vs Rajkumar Maravi on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52436146/
2 9.
So far as income of appellant's is concerned, evidently on the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.6850/-.
Therefore, appellant's income is determined as Rs.6850/- per month.

10. In view of age of appellant 40% is to be added for future prospect and multiplier of 18 is to be applied.
11.
Perusal of impugned award reveal that tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- for loss of income during treatment period.
In view of monthly income of appellant, appellant is entitled to receive Rs.13,700/- (Rs.6850/- x 2) for loss of income during treatment period.
12. Tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/- for pain and suffering.
Under head of pain and suffering appellant is entitled to receive Rs.25,000/-.
Tribunal has not awarded any amount for loss of amenities.

In view of law laid down of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011)1 SCC 343,
appellant is entitled to receive Rs.1,00,000/- for loss of amenities.
